target: - Verify enabled rules, indicator parameter names, required intervals, warmup, execution-bar continuity, and funding coverage before interpreting zero trades or returns. A comparison harness must prepare the union of every candidate's intervals and maximum warmup, or build each candidate separately. Missing data must not masquerade as a strategy with no signals.
content:
- For recursive-indicator parity audits, inspect the actual receiver's input count and closed/forming alignment, not only the acquisition warmup or live minimum. On 2026-10-03, the historical receiver used max(DefaultWarmupBars=200, TechnologyKlineLimit), whereas live's baseline was 150; an audit assuming 149 closed bars mismatched every RG0 ATR/ADX value until recomputed from the actual 199 closed bars. Use the same canonical input window/end/index and unchanged tolerance, preserve failed diagnostics, and distinguish auditing with the original indicator functions from an independent mathematical implementation; fresh snapshots do not prove sequential-cache or live parity.
- Distinguish genuine funding timestamps/rates from settlement-mark completeness. Inspect the original engine's missing-mark policy and report applied fallback counts separately: on 2026-10-03, mark<=0 used the observed funding-minute Close, and an old official response returned an empty mark. Reproduce and label that approximation for original-engine comparisons, without zero funding, synthetic precise marks or silent runtime/source repair. A passed accounting audit does not prove exact exchange settlement prices or all real-cost release gates; preserve missing-mark/source evidence and verify current code before reuse.

- When continuing this user's iterative strategy research after a usage interruption, give a phase summary before starting another experiment: completed versions and full replay counts, passed/failed/pending release gates, failure reasons and evidence limits, portable JSON/report locations, actual process status, and the next concrete research action. Read the latest project checkpoint and recheck the actual goal and process state; stale checkpoint descriptions do not authorize restarting a completed run or resuming a paused goal. Preserve real handles for unfinished work, update the checkpoint when a run or audit actually terminates, and distinguish phase completion from achieving the complete strategy objective. This preamble is scoped to research continuations, not unrelated requests.

target: - Read the current replay engine and dataset builder. Record exact dates, engine/resolution version, data hash, full strategy snapshots, leverage, sizing, both-side fee/slippage assumptions, and actual historical funding. The standard engine evaluates observed minute-close data and fills pending orders at the next minute open. Preserve the outer close gates and validate signal-confirmed exits before releasing a strategy; ROI-only programs may be labeled diagnostic controls, never silently substituted for the final contract.
content: - For a declared exit-only comparison, verify the full enabled entry objects, order and technology are unchanged, then independently replay the complete portfolio path on the same window, coins, data, risk and costs. Different holding times change occupancy, future entries and compounded sizing; deleting old exits or trade groups is descriptive attribution, not the new candidate's PnL.

content: - When changing a directional price/quote admission rule, declare explicit LONG and SHORT numeric expectations, then update both the actual expression and its independent synthetic/canonical oracle. Include strict majority equality, quote legality, price direction and unused forming-field cases. Avoid chained text substitutions that can cancel each other or deriving the oracle solely from the transformed program; preserve initial failures and immutable candidate hashes, and do not launch returns until rule-versus-oracle disagreements are resolved.

target: - Apply the user's frequency gate separately to every coin using the full requested calendar exposure, not just active weeks. Report net and gross PnL, fees, funding, profit factor, drawdown, and yearly/side/symbol concentration. Opposite-direction strategies can both lose after costs; do not infer a tradable inverse edge from net losses alone.
content: - For a multi-version execution/cost audit, retain the aggregate nonzero failure count and every failed row, then attribute focus-candidate versus control failures using the exact full snapshot version and immutable study/dataset identity, not names or row offsets. Report each scope's counts, arithmetic, zero-activity fills and mark fallbacks separately. A preserved control failure need not erase valid focus-candidate diagnostics, but never relabel the whole audit as passed, delete a failed fill or add its net back. Conversely, a candidate's failed execution gate cannot be dismissed as a control issue; even a clean own-minute audit does not prove precise settlement marks, capacity, stability or cross-coin release gates.
